title: Describe anything
hints: Write `switch x := v.(type) { ... }`. In a case with a single type, `x` has that type (`len(x)` works for `[]int`); in a case listing several types, `x` stays an `any`, which `%v` still prints fine.

Follow the rules table top to bottom: `case nil:` first, then `case int:`, `case int8, int16, int32, int64:`, … and `case fmt.Stringer:` near the end so concrete types are matched first. `default:` handles the rest with `fmt.Sprintf("unknown %T", x)`.

The string case is `fmt.Sprintf("string %q with %d runes", x, utf8.RuneCountInString(x))`. A nil `[]int` stored in an `any` has a type, so it reaches `case []int:` and `len(x)` is 0. The Stringer case is `return "stringer " + x.String()`.
